name: conducting-self-review
description: "Use when: Self-review a research plan, analysis, thesis chapter or manuscript before external review; check completeness, internal consistency, traceability and unsupported claims."
---

# Conducting Self-Review

## Procedure
1. Freeze or identify the reviewed artifact version and study stage. Read the problem statement, protocol, relevant outputs and claim/source register; record unavailable inputs.
2. Restate the contribution and strongest claim in neutral language. Check alignment with the question, objectives, scope and actual completed work.
3. Audit internal consistency: definitions, units, sample counts, table/figure values, equations, citations, protocol deviations and planned versus executed analyses. Trace material numerical claims to actual outputs, not remembered values.
4. Use `red-teaming-a-result` for scientific validity checks where results exist. Use method-appropriate counterexamples, interpretive checks or proof review for nonstatistical work. Do not claim an audit of unavailable raw data or code.
5. Examine novelty overclaims, selective reporting, omitted contrary evidence, generalization, causal wording and uncertainty. Ask what evidence would most weaken the conclusion and whether it has been addressed.
6. Classify findings as blocking, major, minor or question, with exact locator, rationale, evidence, proposed action and verification criterion. Label suggestions as suggestions, not discovered defects.
7. Fix clear authorized reversible errors, preserve the pre-review version and log changes. Do not invent experiments, citations or outcomes to fill gaps. Recheck affected claims and record unresolved items.

## Deliver
Write `self-review.md` using the shared review record described in the research workflow, plus a change/response log. Report ready-for-next-review, revise-first or insufficient-material, with scope and limitations.

## Boundaries
Self-review is the author's internal check, not independent peer review. A clean checklist is not proof of correctness or publication readiness. Do not erase contradictory findings or quietly rewrite preregistered decisions.
